Guidance: Patroni relies entirely on the DCS (etcd/Consul/ZooKeeper) for leader election; running an even-numbered or under-sized DCS cluster (e.g. 2 nodes) can't tolerate a single node failure without losing quorum.
Do: Run an odd-numbered DCS cluster (3 or 5 nodes) sized to tolerate the expected failure domain, separate from the Postgres nodes' failure domain where possible.
Don't: Run etcd as a single node or an even-numbered cluster backing a production Patroni setup.

Guidance: TTL/loop_wait/retry_timeout values copied from a tutorial without tuning to your network's actual latency cause either too-slow failover (long outage) or too-aggressive failover (flapping on transient blips).
Do: Tune ttl, loop_wait, and retry_timeout based on observed DCS round-trip latency, balancing failover speed against false-positive failovers.
Don't: Leave Patroni's default timing values unexamined regardless of actual network/DCS latency characteristics.

Keywords: patronictl failover, patronictl switchover, planned maintenance
Guidance: Using 'failover' for planned maintenance treats it like an emergency (no coordination with the current leader), risking a lost transaction; 'switchover' coordinates a clean handoff instead.
Do: Use patronictl switchover for planned leader changes and reserve failover for genuine unplanned leader loss.
Don't: Run patronictl failover for routine planned maintenance instead of switchover.

Guidance: Without a configured watchdog device or fencing mechanism, a network-partitioned old leader that can't reach the DCS may keep accepting writes as if it were still primary, causing data divergence.
Do: Configure a watchdog (Linux softdog or hardware) so Patroni can self-fence a partitioned node that fails to demote in time.
Don't: Run Patroni with no watchdog configured in an environment where network partitions are plausible.

Guidance: Restarting a Postgres node directly with systemctl/pg_ctl instead of through patronictl bypasses Patroni's coordination, risking a confusing state where Patroni's view of the cluster diverges from reality.
Do: Use patronictl restart/reinit/list for all cluster operations so Patroni's state machine stays consistent with actual node status.
Don't: Restart the postgres process directly with systemctl instead of going through patronictl.
Example: patronictl list mycluster\npatronictl restart mycluster node1

Guidance: Enabling synchronous_mode improves durability (no acknowledged write is lost on failover) but means the cluster can't accept writes at all if the synchronous standby is unavailable -- a direct availability/durability trade-off.
Do: Enable synchronous_mode only when zero data loss is a hard requirement, and understand it can block writes during standby outages.
Don't: Enable synchronous replication without evaluating its availability impact when the sync standby goes down.

Keywords: patroni rest api, /health, haproxy health check, liveness
Guidance: Pointing a load balancer's health check at the Postgres port directly (instead of Patroni's REST API) can't distinguish a healthy replica from the actual leader, routing writes to the wrong node.
Do: Use Patroni's REST API endpoints (/leader, /replica, /health) for HAProxy/load balancer health checks, not a raw Postgres port check.
Don't: Configure HAProxy to health-check the raw Postgres TCP port instead of Patroni's role-aware REST endpoints.

Guidance: Bootstrap parameters (initdb options, pg_hba.conf rules) are only applied when a cluster is first initialized; changing them later in the Patroni config has no effect on an already-bootstrapped cluster.
Do: Get bootstrap.dcs settings (pg_hba, initdb params) right before first initialization -- they require manual intervention to change after the fact.
Don't: Assume changing bootstrap-section YAML after the cluster is already running will retroactively apply those settings.
Example:
bootstrap:
  dcs:
    postgresql:
      pg_hba: ["host replication replicator 10.0.0.0/24 md5"]

Keywords: maximum_lag_on_failover, replica promotion, data loss window
Guidance: With no maximum_lag_on_failover set, Patroni can promote a badly lagging replica during failover, silently accepting a larger data-loss window than intended.
Do: Set maximum_lag_on_failover to bound how far behind a replica can be and still be eligible for promotion.
Don't: Leave maximum_lag_on_failover unset and let any replica, however far behind, be eligible for promotion.

Keywords: patronictl pause, maintenance mode, manual dba intervention
Guidance: Performing manual DBA maintenance on a Patroni-managed node without pausing the cluster first risks Patroni 'fixing' your manual change mid-operation, fighting against the DBA.
Do: Use patronictl pause before manual maintenance that Patroni shouldn't interfere with, and resume afterward.
Don't: Perform manual failover testing or config changes on a live node without pausing Patroni first.
Example: patronictl pause mycluster\n# ... manual work ...\npatronictl resume mycluster

Topic: Separating DCS and database failure domains
Keywords: failure domain, dcs placement, availability zone
Guidance: Co-locating the etcd cluster and Postgres nodes on the exact same hosts/AZ means a single AZ failure takes down both the database and its own coordination layer simultaneously.
Do: Spread DCS nodes across different failure domains (AZs) than -- or at least independently from -- the Postgres nodes they coordinate.
Don't: Run etcd nodes on the exact same 3 hosts as the 3 Postgres nodes with no independent failure domain separation.
Example: # etcd on 3 AZs, patroni postgres nodes on 3 AZs, ideally offset

Guidance: Permanent replication slots for a standby that's been offline for a while retain WAL indefinitely on the primary, which can fill the primary's disk if the standby never reconnects.
Do: Monitor replication slot lag/retained WAL size, and remove permanent slots for standbys that are being decommissioned.
Don't: Leave replication slots for decommissioned or long-dead standbys active indefinitely on the primary.
